 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) has been ruled out against the Trail Blazers on Wednesday.
 Mitchell will be sidelined for the second night of OKC’s back-to-back, which will open up a spot in the starting unit. Alex Caruso, Micah Peavy and Nique Clifford are all candidates to take on more minutes, with one of them likely to start.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Kenrich Williams, Aday Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Williams, who played 26 minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers, returns to the starting lineup. As a result, Alex Caruso will come off the bench after making a spot start in Portland. The other four starters are unchanged. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is out for Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Mitchell will miss a second straight game with an ankle injury. Alex Caruso started Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers and should hold onto that role. He is worth streaming with Mitchell out. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is questionable to play against the Clippers on Friday. 
 Mitchell missed Wednesday’s game against Portland, which allowed Alex Caruso to slide into the starting unit. Caruso contributed 14 points, three steals and four triples in the loss and would be worth streaming if Mitchell ends up missing another game. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 The Thunder didn’t have Ajay Mitchell for Wednesday’s game, opening a spot in the starting lineup for Caruso. He took advantage of the opportunity, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. Caruso’s 14 points were a new season high for him, as he totaled 17 points in the first four games he played upon returning from an ankle injury. If Mitchell remains out for Friday’s game against the Clippers, Caruso would be worth rostering in 14-team leagues and some 12-team leagues. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Alex Caruso, Aday Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 The Thunder have made two changes to the lineup that started Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. With Ajay Mitchell out, Caruso moves into the starting lineup. The other change is Mara, who replaces Kenrich Williams. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell recorded 14 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Mitchell has scored in double figures in five straight and nine of his last 10 games. Injuries that have beset the Thunder this season have created more opportunities for the third-year guard, who is averaging a career-high 18.5 points per game and providing top-100 fantasy value. As long as Mitchell stays healthy, he’s capable of maintaining his current production all season long. 
 Nique Clifford 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #10 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Thunder acquired Nique Clifford from the Kings for two second-round picks. 
 The Thunder need depth after being hit hard by injuries, while Clifford gets a fresh start after falling out of the Kings’ rotation. As a rookie, the 24th overall pick in the 2025 draft averaged 8.6 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 25.1 minutes per game last season. Clifford averaged just over six minutes per game in eight appearances this season. Clifford may have a few more opportunities in Oklahoma City, a franchise that has developed young talent well over the years. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell exploded for a season-high 35 points (14-of-20 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), one rebound and five assists over 30 minutes to lead the Thunder to a 128-97 blowout win over the Grizzlies on Friday. 
 Mitchell topped 20 points for the fifth time in the last six games, delivering his second 30-point effort of the season, as he continues to see an exponentially larger role than originally anticipated for the injury-depleted Thunder, who are currently without Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren. The 24-year-old knocked down 9-of-11, including 3-of-3 from long range, to pour in a game-high 21 first-half points. The Grizzlies had zero answers for the Thunder backcourt as Mitchell, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jared McCain supplied 75 of their 98 points through three quarters. Mitchell has delivered top-50 range fantasy value during the first couple weeks of the season and should be rostered until further notice. The Thunder are back in action with a home matchup against the Wizards on Saturday. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell had 23 points (9-of-17 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Cavaliers on Wednesday. 
 While the Thunder are without multiple starters, it appears they’ll be counting on Mitchell for significant scoring. He has at least 20 points in four of his last five games, showing he may be up to the challenge. Mitchell’s fantasy floor has certainly risen given his situation. OKC will have the day off Thursday before taking on the Grizzlies Friday. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Caruso is back after missing Oklahoma City’s last three games with a sprained ankle. He’ll give the Thunder much-needed wing depth, with two-way contract rookie Josh Dix possibly falling out of the rotation.

 Darryn Peterson put up 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, a block, and four 3-pointers in the 125-118 loss to the Rockets on Friday. 
 The Jazz have let Darryn Peterson go, and we’ve really started to see the Kansas version of Darryn Peterson come into fruition. He has started to carry more of the offense and it’s been looking good for the Jazz. They’ve been in more games, and the team really flows well. He led the team in shot attempts in this one including a big third quarter. Continue to hold and we’ll reassess his value once Lauri and JJJ get back.

 Jalen Johnson had 27 points (11-of-26 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal against the Bulls on Friday. 
 Johnson scored 27 points, but was hardly efficient on 26 attempts from the field. He recorded a triple-double, but also had five turnovers in the overtime loss. Johnson is the Hawks’ franchise leader in triple-doubles. Atlanta has the day off Saturday before a matchup against the Bucks on Sunday.

 Ace Bailey scored 21 points (7-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, and three 3-pointers against the Rockets. 
 Bailey had some big shots in this game which helped keep the Jazz in the game. He was a +10 in a game where they lost by 7. You would want more of the peripheral stats that he’s been able to show this season, but it’s hard to complain with the production he’s given you over the course of the season.

 Center

 Alperen Şengün had a monster 43 points (17-of-24 FGs, 8-of-12 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block and a three in the 125-118 win over the Jazz on Friday.
 Şengün took advantage of the Jazz’s center situation, or lack thereof. He was a monster in this game, and the Jazz had no answers for him at all. He won’t be this good every night, but he had a great performance this season. He is shooting way over what he’s shot at any point in his career from the 3PT line, so that should come down a bit, but he’s having a career at this point and with Durant taking more of a step back, there is a lot more sustainability with what he’s doing.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Josh Giddey had 15 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), 10 rebounds, 14 assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Giddey’s triple-double was his first of the season and his 21st since joining the Bulls. Only Michael Jordan (28) has more in franchise history. Giddey has made at least 44 percent of his attempts in four consecutive games after an early season shooting slump. He and the Bulls will face the Timberwolves on Saturday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Kevin Durant had 22 points (5-of-14 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Jazz on Friday. 
 Durant has been taking a bit of a step back this season, which is remarkable given his age that he’s still averaging 20 points per game. The shot attempts have gone down, the efficiency has gone down, the assists are down, and it’s hard to imagine that it will come back to what it was last season. It’s a good thing for Houston that they haven’t needed him to be that guy, but it looks like father time is starting to catch up with him.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Tari Eason scored 14 points (6-of-13 FGs), 11 rebounds, two assists, and two 3-pointers in win over the Jazz on Friday. 
 Eason got the minutes over Jabari Smith in this game, and he was wreaking havoc in this one. He was in the dunker spots and taking advantage of the Jazz’s lack of a high-level big man defender. It’s not a sign to add Tari Eason but more of a reassurance that he is still a good streamer if you’re looking for rebounds with the potential for a good game.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Norman Powell had 33 points (12-of-19 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in the Bulls’ 125-117 victory over the Hawks on Friday. 
 Powell led the Bulls with 33 points in the overtime victory over the Hawks Friday. The 33-year-old guard helped put the game away with an and-1 that put the Bulls up by five with less than two minutes left in overtime. It was Powell’s second game with at least 30 points this season. The Bulls will take on the Timberwolves on the second night of a back-to-back on Saturday. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Mitchell had 25 points, seven assists and five three-pointers, but was also -20 in 32 minutes in the loss to the Heat on Friday. The 30-year-old guard has scored at least 25 points and made five three-pointers twice in his last four games. The Cavaliers will face the Mavericks at home on the second night of a back-to-back on Saturday.
